title: Polynomial-time approximation for Max-Cut
statement: For every real $\\eta>0$, there is a polynomial-time computable map $A$ from bit strings to bit strings and there are natural numbers $C,k$ with the following property. Whenever a bit string parses as a nonempty list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers, encode each pair in $E$ as an edge of a weighted graph, giving each ordered pair $(u,v)$ weight equal to the total number of occurrences of $(u,v)$ and $(v,u)$ in $E$, divided by twice the length of $E$. The expected cut value of this graph, using the Boolean assignment whose value at vertex $v$ is the $v$th output bit of $A$ on the encoding of the input bit string paired with a uniformly random bit string of length $C(\\lvert\\text{bits}\\rvert+1)^k$ (and using false when that output has no $v$th bit), is at least the Goemans–Williamson constant times the graph’s maximum cut value minus $\\eta$.
hypotheses_covered: The bit string parses to the specified edge list
The random bit string has length $C(\\lvert\\text{bits}\\rvert+1)^k$ and is sampled uniformly
